title_en: Wisdom in Calling People to Islam [1]
body_ar:
تعتبر الدعوة إلى الله سبحانه وتعالى الركيزة الأولى في تثبيت دعائم الدين الإسلامي، لذا أمر الله بها الأنبياء وأتباعهم؛ إذ بدعوتهم قامت الأديان وانتشر توحيد الله في البلدان. وقد تحدث أهل العلم عن الدعوات واستقبال الناس لها على أصنافهم، وعن سبل الدعوة والحكمة فيها، سواءٌ أكانت تلك الحكمة تجاه الأشخاص أم الأوقات أم الأزمان المناسبة لها؛ فإنها ما شرعت إلا لإقامة الدين وتغيير المنكر القائم بين الناس بحكمة وروية، ووضع للأمور في مواضعها.
التذكير بالله والدعوة إليه ضرورة دينية:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعثه ربه رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه، ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. أما بعد: فإن الله عز وجل قد وصف نفسه بالدعوة، فقال سبحانه وتعالى في محكم كتابه: وَاللَّهُ يَدْعُوا إِلَى دَارِ السَّلامِ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ [يونس:25] ، وقال تعالى: أُوْلَئِكَ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى النَّارِ وَاللَّهُ يَدْعُو إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ وَالْمَغْفِرَةِ بِإِذْنِهِ [البقرة:221] . ووصف رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك في قوله تعالى: وَدَاعِيًا إِلَى اللَّهِ بِإِذْنِهِ وَسِرَاجًا مُنِيرًا. [الأحزاب:46]...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Calling people to God, glorified and exalted is He (daʿwah), is held to be the first support in making the pillars of the Islamic religion firm. For this reason God commanded the prophets and their followers to undertake it, since it was by their calling that the religions were established and the affirmation of God's oneness spread through the lands. The people of knowledge have discussed the various calls and the different classes of people in their reception of them, and the ways of the call and the wisdom to be used in it — whether that wisdom concerns the persons addressed, or the hours, or the seasons suited to it. For the call was laid down for no purpose other than to establish the religion and to change the wrong standing among people, with wisdom and deliberation, and by putting matters in their proper places.

## Reminding people of God and calling them to Him is a religious necessity

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one whom his Lord sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed: God, mighty and majestic, has described Himself as calling, for He, glorified and exalted is He, said in the clear text of His Book: {And God calls to the abode of peace, and He guides whom He wills to a straight path} (Sūrat Yūnus 10:25). And He, exalted is He, said: {Those call to the Fire, and God calls to the Garden and to forgiveness by His leave} (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:221). And He described His Messenger, God bless him and grant him peace, in the same terms, in His words, exalted is He: {and as one calling to God by His leave, and as an illuminating lamp} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:46) …

flags.context: the section heading: التذكير بالله والدعوة إليه ضرورة دينية
flags.note: 'ضرورة' is used here in its ordinary sense of 'something indispensable', not in the technical sense of the legal threshold of necessity (ḍarūrah) that permits the otherwise forbidden. The glossary entry for ḍarūrah warns against the technical reading; the heading of a lesson on the duty of calling people to God is not a ruling of necessity, and the English is kept non-technical so that no such reading arises.

flags.context: the site's synopsis, on the prophets' calling

it was by their calling that the revealed religions were established
flags.note: 'الأديان' is plural. In context it means the successive revealed religions brought by the prophets, not religion in general and not the religions of the world at large. Rendered as the plural the Arabic gives, without narrowing it, since the synopsis is the site's wording and not the Sheikh's.

translator_notes: One of a run of six records, IDs 701-706, in the written-da'wah section, all uploaded on 9 May 2011 within about twenty minutes of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/c-c-* series. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lesson was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic.
